prompt.adult: At the wedding in Cana, what stood there according to the manner of purification of the Jews?
prompt.child: At a wedding in Cana, some large containers were standing nearby. What were they?
prompt.teen: John 2:6: “Now there were set there” what?
prompt.older: According to John 2:6, what were set there for purification?

verses.text: Now there were set there six waterpots of stone, according to the manner of purification of the Jews, containing twenty or thirty gallons apiece.

explanation.child: Look near the start of verse 6.
explanation.teen: 2:6 names what was set there, then their purpose and size. Read the first part.
explanation.older: It follows “Now there were set there” in 2:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:6 goes on to say each one contained twenty or thirty gallons.
teaching.takeaway: There were set there six waterpots of stone.

prompt.adult: By a pool in Jerusalem lay a man with an infirmity. According to 5:5, how long had he had it?
prompt.child: Jesus met a sick man lying by a pool. How long had the man been sick?
prompt.teen: John 5:5: “who had an infirmity” how long?
prompt.older: According to John 5:5, how long had the man had an infirmity?

verses.text: Now a certain man was there who had an infirmity thirty-eight years.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 5.
explanation.teen: 5:5 names the man and then how long. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “who had an infirmity” in 5:5.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:6 says Jesus knew he had already been in that condition a long time, and asked, “Do you want to be made well?”
teaching.takeaway: He had an infirmity thirty-eight years.

prompt.adult: Jesus asked Philip, “Where shall we buy bread, that these may eat?” According to 6:6, why did He ask?
prompt.child: Jesus asked Philip where they could buy bread for a big crowd. Why did He ask him?
prompt.older: According to John 6:6, why did Jesus ask Philip the question?

verses.text: Then Jesus lifted up His eyes, and seeing a great multitude coming toward Him, He said to Philip, “Where shall we buy bread, that these may eat?”
But this He said to test him, for He Himself knew what He would do.

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 6.
explanation.teen: 6:6 gives the reason first and then what Jesus knew. Read the reason.
explanation.older: It follows “But this He said” in 6:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: 6:5 says Jesus lifted up His eyes and saw a great multitude coming. 6:6 ends, “for He Himself knew what He would do.”
teaching.takeaway: He said this to test him.

prompt.adult: Jesus anointed a man’s eyes with clay. In 9:7, where did He tell him to go and wash?
prompt.child: Jesus put clay on a blind man’s eyes. Where did He send him to wash?
prompt.older: According to John 9:7, where was the man told to wash?

verses.text: When He had said these things, He spat on the ground and made clay with the saliva; and He anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay.
And He said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which is translated, Sent). So he went and washed, and came back seeing.

explanation.adult: Read Jesus’ words at the start of 9:7.
explanation.child: Look near the start of verse 7.
explanation.teen: 9:7 gives the command, a translation, and then what happened. Read the command.

teaching.extended_explanation: 9:6 says He spat on the ground and made clay with the saliva. 9:7 ends, “and came back seeing.”
teaching.takeaway: He said, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam.”

prompt.adult: The nobleman asked his servants when his son began to get better. According to 4:52, when did the fever leave him?
prompt.child: A father learned his son got well at the same time Jesus spoke. When did the fever leave the boy?
prompt.teen: John 4:52: “Yesterday at” what time “the fever left him”?
prompt.older: According to John 4:52, at what time did the fever leave?

verses.text: Then he inquired of them the hour when he got better. And they said to him, “Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.”
So the father knew that it was at the same hour in which Jesus said to him, “Your son lives.” And he himself believed, and his whole household.

explanation.child: Look at the last part of verse 52.
explanation.teen: 4:52 has his question and then their reply. Read the time in the reply.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:53 says the father knew it was the same time Jesus said, “Your son lives.” He and his whole household believed.
teaching.takeaway: The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour.

prompt.adult: In 11:37 some asked whether Jesus could have kept a man from dying. According to 9:1, how long had the man Jesus saw been blind?
prompt.child: Jesus saw a man who could not see. How long had he been that way?
prompt.teen: John 9:1: “He saw a man who was blind” since when?
prompt.older: Linking John 9:1 with 11:37, how long had the man whose eyes were opened been blind?

verses.text: Now as Jesus passed by, He saw a man who was blind from birth.
And some of them said, “Could not this Man, who opened the eyes of the blind, also have kept this man from dying?”

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 9:1.
explanation.teen: 11:37 is the setting; 9:1 says who He saw and how long. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “a man who was blind” in 9:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 9:1 says this was as Jesus passed by. 11:37 recalls Him as the one “who opened the eyes of the blind.”
teaching.takeaway: He saw a man who was blind from birth.

prompt.adult: John 2:11 calls the sign at Cana the beginning of signs. What does 4:54 call the healing of the nobleman’s son?
prompt.child: What does John call the healing of the official’s son?
prompt.older: Alongside “This beginning of signs” in 2:11, what does 4:54 call this healing?

verses.text: This beginning of signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and manifested His glory; and His disciples believed in Him.
This again is the second sign Jesus did when He had come out of Judea into Galilee.

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 54.
explanation.teen: 2:11 is the setting; 4:54 numbers the sign and then says where He came from. Read the first part.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:11 says He manifested His glory, and His disciples believed in Him. 4:54 says He had come out of Judea into Galilee.
teaching.takeaway: “This again is the second sign Jesus did.”

prompt.adult: In 5:9 the man took up his bed and walked. In 9:14, Jesus made clay and opened the man’s eyes. On what day did both happen?
prompt.child: Two of Jesus’ healings in John happened on a special day. Which day?
prompt.older: Linking John 5:9 with 9:14, on what day were both healings done?

verses.text: And immediately the man was made well, took up his bed, and walked. And that day was the Sabbath.
Now it was a Sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.

explanation.teen: Both verses name the day: 5:9 at its end, and 9:14 at its start. Read either.
explanation.older: It closes 5:9, after “And that day was.”

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:9 says the man was made well immediately. 9:14 says Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.
teaching.takeaway: Both were done on the Sabbath.
